experience_principles.name: Specification Primacy
experience_principles.rule: Specifications remain the primary editing surface; graph state is inspectable but not the primary editing model.

experience_principles.name: Progressive Complexity Disclosure
experience_principles.rule: Users encounter intent, specification, workflow, and outcome before graph, dependency, validation, reconciliation, and topology details.

experience_principles.name: Execution Transparency
experience_principles.rule: Users always know what is happening, completed, blocked, failed, or awaiting action without needing worker orchestration internals.

experience_principles.name: Validation Visibility
experience_principles.rule: Validation failures remain visible and actionable until resolved.

experience_principles.name: Reconciliation Visibility
experience_principles.rule: Reconciliation outcomes remain inspectable even when reconciliation succeeds.

experience_principles.name: Approval Visibility
experience_principles.rule: Approval prompts explain why approval is needed, what changes, and what risk is accepted.

modes.name: Repository Ingestion
hidden_complexity: unconfirmed low-confidence nodes in canonical graph

primary_screen_hierarchy.name: Execution

design_tokens.status_rule: Use color plus explicit icon and text; never color alone.

acceptance_criteria: The graph is visible and inspectable but never the primary editing surface.
Execution visibility emphasizes status, blockers, validation, outputs, and actions rather than internal worker mechanics.
Every status indicator uses both semantic color and explicit text.
Approval review shows reason, scope, impact, traceability, and risk before action.
Validation and reconciliation failures remain visible until resolved.
UI graph has no direct graph mutation action.
